QF.id: AIFM CII AIFs in India and Suitability_1

question.text: Mr. Ramesh Iyer, a new IC member at Lotus Capital AIF (a Category II private equity fund), is preparing an induction note on the Indian AIF industry's regulatory timeline. Which of the following correctly identifies the regulatory watershed that transformed the erstwhile VC/PE industry in India into a full-fledged 'AIF industry' and provided the current legal framework for Cat I and II managers?

answer.text: The notification of the SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012, under which Category I, II and III AIFs are registered
The SEBI (Venture Capital Fund) Regulations, 1996, which first brought unlisted-company investing under SEBI purview
The K.B. Chandrasekhar Committee recommendations of 2000, which introduced fund-level tax pass-through for VCFs
The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, which created the operating space for Special Situations Funds

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 3, growth in the Indian alternatives industry picked up from 2012 due to the SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012. The 2011-2019 period is described as the phase during which the erstwhile VC/PE industry transformed into a full-fledged AIF industry, and AIFs are currently regulated under the SEBI AIF Regulations, 2012, with Category I, II and III registrations. The Trap: The SEBI (Venture Capital Fund) Regulations, 1996 are historically important for unlisted-company investing but pre-date and were superseded by the 2012 AIF framework. The K.B. Chandrasekhar Committee recommendations of 2000 are a historical input to VCF policy, not the founding regulation of the AIF industry. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 created the operating space for stressed-asset strategies but does not itself constitute the AIF regulatory framework. Note: The watershed event for the modern AIF industry is the 2012 AIF Regulations, under which Category I, II and III AIFs are registered today.
